title: LMT or HWM: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
author: Na
description: In a comparison of two Aerospace-Defense sector stocks, Lockheed Martin (LMT) and Howmet (HWM), both holding a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), LMT emerges as the superior value option. LMT has a forward P/E of 16.64 and PEG ratio of 1.10, compared to HWM's 43.06 and 2.07 respectively. LMT received a Value grade of B versus HWM's D grade, making it the more attractive choice for value investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: LMT demonstrates superior valuation metrics with a lower forward P/E ratio (16.64 vs 43.06), lower PEG ratio (1.10 vs 2.07), and a stronger Value grade (B vs D). Both stocks share a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), but LMT's fundamentals make it the better value option for investors.

HWM holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) indicating positive earnings outlook, but its valuation metrics are less attractive than LMT. With a higher forward P/E (43.06), higher PEG ratio (2.07), and weaker Value grade (D), it is considered less favorable for value investors despite solid fundamentals.

title: Strength in Aerospace & Defense Drives RBC Bearings: Can It Sustain?
author: Na
description: RBC Bearings' Aerospace & Defense segment revenues surged 36.9% in fiscal Q1 2027 to $225.4 million, driven by commercial aerospace growth (21.8%) and robust defense demand (64.6%). The company projects Q2 sales of $505-$515 million with 10.9%-13.1% year-over-year growth, supported by a $2.3 billion backlog and strong U.S. defense budgetary provisions.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong revenue growth of 36.9% in Aerospace & Defense segment, robust backlog of $2.3 billion, solid guidance for Q2 with double-digit growth, and positive momentum across both commercial aerospace and defense markets driven by higher aircraft build rates and government defense spending.
Positive momentum in defense sector with robust orders for engine spares for legacy fighters; defense aerospace revenues surged 11% year-over-year in Q2, supported by steady government support.

Defense & Propulsion Technologies segment revenues increased 16% year-over-year to $3.4 billion in Q2 2026, benefiting from healthy demand for propulsion, additive technologies, critical aircraft systems, and aftermarket services in the defense market.
